items.text: IS THAT KICK KNOCKING AT THE DOOR OR DEMOLISHING THE HOUSE?!
Everything sounds enormous! Even the shortage of ideas!
Where are the contrasts? A locomotive has ironed this music flat!
That crescendo climbs a long way to reach an empty chair.
The melody should confront the bass, not hide under the carpet!
What a timid entrance! Let the theme barge in shoulders first!
The volume has muscles. Expression stayed in the changing room.
The same rhythm again? Even storms find new ways to be furious!
They compressed the drama until it fitted in a tin!
That pause builds no tension. It sounds like someone hunting for a socket.
That outburst had force! It knocked down me and nearly the music stand!
THUNDER AND BLAST! The melody fought back. I respect notes with fists.
I lost... but that contrast made me leap out of my chair. The chair is my witness!
The bass has drive. It can be pleased: it drove me straight into defeat.
That silence before the entrance... Yes, it worked. DO NOT MAKE ME REPEAT IT!
The chorus has character. Insufferable character, but character!
There was emotion under all that noise. I had to excavate, but it was there!
That motif grew! Too much: it ran me over.
The dynamics breathed. I am gasping now, but they breathed!
I withdraw no complaint about the volume. I only admit the music had fire!
VICTORY! Volume cannot do the composer's job!
The kick hit hard. The theme should have struck first!
That crescendo swelled until it burst. Musical confetti!
Contrast has won! Someone explain it to the compressor!
All that energy, only to finish like a drum without a skin!
I won before that melody found its courage!
The chorus demanded power. It needed a reason to shout!
That settles it! Drama has defeated the blender!
A hundred speakers could not save a theme that tiptoes!
A forceful ending! Mine. Theirs is still looking for the button.
What a discreet melody! It passed through my head without leaving an address.
That chord returns so often we should charge it rent.
The chorus is sticky. So is jam on a keyboard.
They put sequins on a scale and called it a solo.
Such conversation between instruments! They all say “me” at once.
The theme promised wit. I assume the promise was not binding.
That bridge is so short it cannot cross a puddle.
The voice has so many touch-ups the original might have been a flute.
A harmonic surprise! Oh, no. The same chord in a hat.
So much rhythm to take such a lazy idea for a walk.
The melody has wit. It beat me before I finished the insult. Bad manners!
That instrumental answer was brilliant. I know: it left me without a comeback.
The hook works. You may remove it from my wig now.
Good harmonic surprise! My face performed an involuntary modulation.
That bridge led somewhere. Unfortunately, to my competitive funeral.
The arrangement had wit. I demand a rematch with less talent.
The phrase was simple and neatly resolved. An offensively effective combination.
That vocal dialogue made me laugh. Defeat is less amusing.
I admit the rhythm has charm. Do not give it my seat as well.
The chorus is memorable. Now I have to remember losing. Thanks for that.
I won! That same chord can go back to looking for work.
The hook failed to catch victory. Try an interesting note.
What a surprise! The shortage of ideas had consequences.
That solo went down the scale. I suppose it is leaving.
The chorus will return. I shall have finished celebrating.
All those touch-ups, and they could not tune the result!
A lazy idea just lost to one that got up early.
The bridge collapsed. Luckily, development had never stepped onto it.
Victory is mine! Anyone care to adopt that homeless melody?
We can repeat the match. The song has plenty of experience repeating itself.
Three!
Two!
One!
Tempo!
Fury!
Perfect!
Three!
Two!
One!
Tempo!
Fury!
Perfect!
One lonely melody? This is counterpoint on strike!
That bass is repeating a year. And failing every bar.
So many tracks, and not one voice listens to the others!
This harmony has weaker foundations than an inflatable organ.
Where is the answer to the subject? Lost in the corridor?
A filter is no substitute for modulation, however much it goes whee-whee.
These voices only stay together because someone glued them.
The kick keeps time. Everything else seems to misplace it.
This is no fugue: it is a theme looking for the exit.
I looked for development. All I found was a repeat button.
The bass supports the voices well... I resent having to certify it.
That entrance was well placed. Who taught the machine discipline?
A simple structure beat me. Simple, but well built. How irritating.
The layers fit. It is no counterpoint, but at least they avoid stepping on toes.
I admit that tension resolved well. I shall record it in small print.
The rhythm is solid. Unfortunately, so is the result.
That imitation between instruments made sense. Who authorized it?
I followed the bass to the end. Not one blunder. Suspicious.
The chorus has impeccable logic. I would like to file a complaint.
Few notes, good voice leading... I lost, but I found order.
Case closed: stacking noises does not produce counterpoint.
The whole building collapsed. The bass was meant to be a foundation, not a cushion!
The chorus returned. Victory did not return with it.
A decent cadence might have helped. So might a miracle.
The voices were not speaking. Now they can share the silence.
Order, harmony, and one perfectly catalogued victory!
That chord wanted resolution. It got defeat instead.
The theme failed to develop. The disaster, however, flourished.
Another loop for the failed exercises drawer!
You may switch off the metronome. The verdict is in.
That motif is a seed. Why serve it without planting it?
Another layer of sound will not give this idea substance.
The bass and melody live like neighbours who never say hello.
This rhythm needs a syncopation. Or very strong coffee.
They varnished the orchestration before building the table.
Why rush to the chorus? Is dinner waiting?
The theme returns untouched. Not a wrinkle from doing any work!
This accompaniment is so light a sneeze could carry it away.
Harmony offers a door. The song prefers circling the landing.
All that outward polish, and the motif is still in pyjamas.
They developed the motif sensibly. A pity for my bad mood.
That cross-rhythm had substance. It tied my victory in knots.
The inner voices were good. Yes, I listen to the middle ones too.
The harmony knew where it was going. I was heading for victory, but took a wrong turn.
I admit the theme's return was well prepared. Irritatingly well prepared.
The texture had weight. All of it landed on me.
That variation was clever. The defeat seems less well written.
Those chords had warmth. No, I am not asking for a hug.
An economical melody, well used. My complaint has gone over budget.
The ending gathered every idea. And my victory too, apparently.
Substance won. The varnish can go back in the tin.
The motif never grew. We harvested precisely one crumb.
A solid victory! The opposing accompaniment still needs scaffolding.
All those repetitions, and not one variation worth the journey!
The bass went its own way. It reached defeat all by itself.
The race to the chorus is over. There was no prize.
A rhythm with two legs walks better than one with a single crutch!
The texture made a bulky parcel. Nothing inside the box.
I won through development. A job the loop had left until tomorrow.
Matter closed. That harmony needs proper foundations and less glitter.
That kick entered the drawing room in muddy boots.
The melody needs air. The compressor put it in a corset.
Where is the rubato? Even the curtains move more freely.
Those ornaments look like sugar tipped straight from the sack.
All that electronic sustain, and not one well-phrased sigh.
The voice slides between notes like a spoon on an empty plate.
Such delicate cymbals. They served the crockery with a shovel.
That accompaniment steps on the melody and still asks it to dance.
A nocturne under those lights? Not even a moth could sleep.
The notes arrive on time. Grace missed the carriage.
That phrase breathed tastefully. I fear I have lost elegantly.
The bass was discreet and effective. Manners I did not expect to find here.
There was a lovely nuance. I heard it before making this face.
The melody had cantabile. How inconsiderate of my prejudices.
That expressive delay was well judged. The defeat was far too punctual.
I admit the ornament enhanced the phrase. It need not have embellished my defeat too.
The texture left room for the voice. I would have sat there, had I not fallen first.
That chord had tenderness. Please do not announce it with a kick drum.
The pulse was flexible. My disapproval has had to bend too.
The ending was delicate. It almost had the courtesy not to humiliate me.
Nuance won. You may remove the boots from the drawing room.
The melody needed to breathe. Now it has all the silence it wanted.
Such a stiff defeat. The metronome must be proud.
The ornament failed to cover the emptiness. It merely framed it in lace.
A victory without raising my voice. Do try it sometime.
That intrusive accompaniment may escort defeat to the door.
Sensitivity cannot be purchased with reverb. What a revelation.
I have won. The plate has finally stopped fighting the spoon.
So many sliding notes, and not one landed gracefully.
One final recommendation: less hammering on the imaginary piano, more music.
That entrance calls for a fanfare, not an ambitious toaster!
That choir is so small I could summon it with a teaspoon.
A chorus should proclaim something. This one announces its own return.
Such solemnity! The coronation of a bicycle bell.
The echo answers more confidently than the lead singer.
That bass walks as though carrying a tray of jellies.
The voice takes so many turns it has forgotten the aria.
They have confused grandeur with switching on every trumpet at once.
Where is the dialogue between soloist and ensemble? I hear only a shouting meeting.
That cadence needs ceremony. Not an endless queue of effects.
The chorus gathers the voices well. They had the insolence to sound majestic.
That entrance had authority. It made me stand before I lost.
The bass supported the whole ensemble. Work worthy of payment, regrettably.
I found nobility in that melody. Who let it in without an invitation?
The alternating voices worked. Even my protest waited its turn.
That climax had splendour. I refuse to order it a crown.
The voice ornamented sensibly. Not with a watering can, as I feared.
The rhythm had a convincing march. It paraded me straight into defeat.
I admit the ending was resounding. So was my groan.
This ensemble breathes as one. Very well. Nobody shout hallelujah yet.
Sound the trumpets! The in-tune ones, preferably!
Grandeur has triumphed. The toaster may return to the kitchen.
That choir proclaimed nothing. Except unanimous defeat.
The fanfare ran out of breath. The verdict still has lungs!
They crowned volume and dethroned melody. A predictable result!
A solemn victory! Reserve a small chair for that chorus.
The voice sought glory. It found an unflattering ending.
That bass could not even support the concert programme!
The ceremony is over. You may pick the effects up off the floor.
An ovation for harmony! The smoke machine has had enough applause.
The chorus again? Surprise must be stuck in traffic.
That silence promised a joke. All we got was more kick drum.
Theme and answer wear the same hat. How do we tell them apart?
The form is square. A pity music is not a footstool.
That ending announces itself so often I have sent it an invitation.
An unexpected modulation, please! Even the soup tureen can make a turn.
The phrase asked a question. The next one answered with a yawn.
That symmetry is impeccable. So is the symmetry of two closed doors.
The bass makes the same joke every bar. We got it the first time.
All that preparation, only to come in through the usual door!
That accent surprised me. A well-placed joke; I get to be the audience.
The form was neatly tied together. I tripped over it with complete dignity.
That pause had wit. Apparently I was today's joke.
The theme's return caught me smiling. Inadmissible evidence!
A good answer to that phrase. My defence answered late.
The dynamic play was lively. Victory skipped right out of my hands.
That modulation was amusing. Not as amusing as my face when I heard it.
The ending knew how to keep us waiting. I was waiting to win, as it happens.
The motif was small but shrewd. It picked my musical pocket.
I admit the rhythm played well with expectations. Mine are on the floor.
Surprise! A witless structure can still lose right on time.
The theme returned unchanged. The result gave it something new!
What a timely pause. I can finally celebrate in peace.
The music had no turns. Victory still found its way.
An ending announced twenty bars in advance. And they still look surprised!
The phrase asked who would win. I kindly supplied the answer.
The bass repeated its joke until it lost the humour and the match.
Victory! A little wit dismantled that wardrobe full of choruses.
I supplied the unexpected accent: right on the victory.
Everything so neatly squared... A pity the result does not fit.
The voice says one thing, the harmony another. What a madrigal of misunderstandings!
That vocal effect is wearing a mask. Bring the real voice onstage!
A dissonance should pierce the heart, not tickle the cable.
Where is the gesture in the phrase? This declaims like an automatic door.
The melody falls to its knees while the bass keeps mopping the floor!

The rhythm will not let the singer speak. Even servants interrupt less!
That entrance needs intention, not a smoke curtain with pitch.
They dressed emotion in effects and gave it no role.
Basso continuo does not mean a bass that continually annoys!
That harmonic turn served the expression. I acknowledge it, irritating though it is.
The voice made a convincing gesture. I made the gesture of losing.
That dissonance knew when to yield. My indignation is still rehearsing.
The bass let the melody declaim. Courtesy I did not expect.
There was theatre in that entrance. And I ended up backstage.
I admit the voices conversed. They even agreed on how to defeat me.
The effect highlighted emotion. It did not hide it. I must revise my complaint.
That pause said something. Right now I would rather say very little.
The phrase had dramatic direction. It led me to an undignified exit.
The melody knew how to move us. Let the record show my grimace is expressive too.
Curtain down! The artificial voice may remove its makeup.
Expression won. The effects can be extras.
The dissonance said nothing. Defeat was very eloquent.
That bass has interrupted the aria for the last time!
A short tragedy: the melody went onstage without intention.
The doubled vocals may now share a single defeat.
Victory! It takes no thirty filters to make a note speak.

So you're the one who beat my students? I was here before the first note.
Bach, Mozart, Wagner... they all asked my permission. You didn't even knock.
That song of yours... I discarded it ten thousand years ago. Too predictable.
I am do, re and mi at once. You are, at best, background noise.
Before rhythm existed, I was already tapping my feet. Shall we?

Silence is music too. You're about to hear plenty of it.

Hm. An unexpected chord. I liked it... a little.
You played in time. Three times in a row. I'll make a note.
I didn't see that syncopation coming. And I see everything coming.
Fine, fine: you've got more rhythm than you look.
First bar to you. The score is still long.

Good. You've mastered C major. Now comes the tricky one.

A perfect cadence... against me. The nerve.

Again? Of course. Music always returns to the theme.
Sorry, I wrote this ending.

You lost the beat. I'll keep it: every beat is mine.
Not a high C. Not a C of any kind.
Bravo! Oh no, that was the echo of my own bravo.

Every note you play, I've played before. And better.
Today I'll modulate to a key that doesn't have a name yet.
The metronome is mine. And right now it's speeding up.
I've got eighty violins inside me. All of them out of tune against you.

Get ready for a crescendo that never ends.
No rests this time. Everything fortissimo.
You survived my tutti. Few live to tell.

Fine. You deserve a seventh chord. No more.
You made me miss my cue. Me. I AM every cue.
I accept defeat like a fermata: brief and elegant.

Second movement to you. The third is my favourite.
You found the blue note. And I'd hidden it so well.
Alright: you can join my band. Tambourine, for now.
You made the harmony resonate. It tickles.
The symphony ends when I say so. And I say so now.
Too many notes, too few ideas.
You tripped on a 7/8 bar. A classic.
I enjoyed your defeat. It had a good tempo.
The whole hall is silent. Out of respect. For me.
You played with feeling. The wrong feeling.

Don't worry: history will remember you as a footnote.
Your solo lasted less than a glissando.
You'll be back. Everyone returns to the tonic in the end.

The stars vibrate at my frequency. You'll vibrate too.
Before the Big Bang there was a count-in. I called it.
This is my final form: every song at once.
Every time anyone hummed, it was me. Now I hum against you.

Sorry, there's no pause button here. There never was.

Incredible. You beat me... and it still sounded good.
Alright. From now on, whenever someone sings in the shower, I'll think of you.

A standing ovation from the galaxies. They're very loud, galaxies.

Bring down the curtain. And don't touch anything: the piano is mine.
The universe remains in tune. Thanks for taking part.
You came close. A semitone, at most.
Music always wins. It's in the name.
Start again from the first bar. I'll wait for you at the end.
Nice try. I'll put it on a compilation of oddities.
You lost to a concept. The concept is delighted.
The stars are laughing in C major.
You were my favourite note today. The only one, actually.
Don't worry: even Beethoven needed nine symphonies.

voices.refText: Quiet! Quiet, I said! You call that music? Listen. It starts softly, very softly... and then it hits you right in the face!
Ha! Too slow, too slow! I wrote three symphonies while you were tying your shoes. Come on, keep up, it's only getting faster!
Three! Two! One! Let's go! Welcome to the arena, where every beat hits like a punch. Are you ready? Here we go!
Three! Two! One! Let's go! Welcome to the arena, where every beat hits like a punch. Are you ready? Here we go!
Every voice has its place, and every place has its voice. Listen carefully: four lines, one purpose. Now, shall we begin the lesson?
I have waited a long time for this. Patience, my friend. A good symphony takes twenty years. A good fight, perhaps a little less.
Shh... not so loud. Music is a whisper, not a shout. Let the melody breathe, bend the time a little, and then... it dances away.
Ladies and gentlemen, the curtain rises! Bigger, louder, more trumpets! When I enter a hall, the whole of London stands up!
Ah, good evening! Sit down, relax, enjoy the music. Nice and calm, nice and calm... and then, surprise! Did I wake you up?
Behold the stage! Every word must sing, every silence must weep. Tonight, my friend, we invent the drama all over again!
I am every note you have ever heard, and every silence between them. You have played well. Now listen to what music truly is.
The same eight notes. Again. And again. You may tire of them. I never will. Patience is a canon, and the canon always returns.
Can you feel it? The swans, the snow, the cannons! Everything at once! Oh, music is too beautiful to be gentle!
Spring, summer, autumn, winter! Faster, faster! The violins are flying, the storm is coming, and I have five hundred concertos left!
Silence. You stand before an epic. Four evenings, fifteen hours, gods and fire. Do not expect this to be short.
